contentBlocks.text: This week you went beyond Grade 9's rhetoric basics into genuinely advanced analysis. Let's review it all!

Quick review: rhetorical structure is the strategic order of ideas, often building to a climax (Day 1). Audience adaptation tailors rhetoric to a specific audience's values (Day 2). Appeals often work together, reinforcing each other (Day 3). You combined all three into one complete written analysis (Day 4). Explain in your own words why analyzing HOW a text is built (structure, audience, combined appeals) matters more for a skilled reader than just identifying WHAT appeals are present.
Great work this week — you moved from Grade 9's rhetoric basics to genuinely advanced analysis! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review rhetorical structure, audience adaptation, and combined appeals
Explain why analyzing HOW a text is built matters more than just identifying WHAT appeals are present
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child explain why HOW matters more than just WHAT.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of advanced rhetorical analysis!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the skill the child found most interesting this week (often audience adaptation) rather than requiring an even summary of all three
Ready for more: ask the child how they might use this week's skills (structure, audience adaptation) in their own future persuasive writing, not just in analyzing someone else's
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's three advanced rhetorical-analysis skills needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: Simply identifying WHAT appeals are present (this is ethos, this is pathos) only labels the pieces — understanding HOW a text is built (why this order, why this emphasis for this audience, why these appeals reinforce each other) reveals the actual craft and strategy behind a persuasive text, which is a much deeper, more useful skill for both analyzing others' writing and improving one's own.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Common Core Grade 11-12 rhetorical-analysis standards (RI.11-12.6) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
